memories.content: Use the same term throughout the proposal for the same interaction concept or interface element.
Use abbreviations only for recurring terms of three or more words.
Present the full name and abbreviation together when using an abbreviation for the first time.
Prioritize the research role over diagnostic labels or deficits when referring to participants.
Reviewers from different subfields struggle to infer undefined abbreviations from context alone.
Use the term formative evaluation for studies seeking design modification evidence, and distinguish it from final efficacy judgments.
The user can have contribution labels such as principles, models, or guidelines approved only if they align with the abstraction level of the actual deliverables.
Design principles describe the relationship between conditions and outcomes rather than serving as instructions that merely replicate a single screen layout.
Calculate user research compensation budgets based on the estimated participation burden, combining session time with required technical and travel preparation.
Compensate participants who withdraw from the study midway for their actual participation time.
Compensate for the time actually spent in sessions, regardless of the research modality.
Allow the issuance of gift cards of equivalent value to participants in remote studies who cannot use electronic transfers.
Do not treat an unresolved payment method as a deficiency at the proposal stage.
Allow differential compensation amounts for on-site and remote studies when participation burden varies due to travel or technical preparation.
Participants judge the fairness of compensation based on the combined burden of session time and required technical and travel preparation.
In longitudinal studies requiring diary entries and repeated reporting, include out-of-session recording time in compensation calculations.
Distinguish between participant research compensation and labor costs for field staff performing installation and operational support as part of their duties.
The user tends to count session time but omit participants’ advance setup and follow-up reporting time.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate operational domains: the reference frame governs proposal terminology, participant-centered wording, study labels, and contribution framing, while the compared frame governs participant compensation, burden accounting, payment methods, withdrawal, modality, and staff-cost boundaries. No shared or conflicting policy is present.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame addresses burden-based compensation, withdrawal and longitudinal work, modality differences, payment alternatives, proposal-stage uncertainty, and the separation of participant payments from staff labor costs.
reports.reference_only: The reference frame sets proposal-language rules for consistent terminology, abbreviations, respectful participant descriptions, formative evaluation, and appropriately abstract contribution labels and design principles.
